flagship.name: AION
flagship.summary: Classic operating systems schedule CPU and RAM for programs. AION schedules the resources AI agents actually run out of — tokens, context, and credits.
flagship.description: A zero-dependency micro-kernel that gives autonomous agents OS-grade primitives: a content-addressed virtual filesystem (skip re-reading unchanged files by hash), semantic long-term memory, transparent read caching, per-process credit budgets, capability-based sandboxing, a package manager, and inter-process messaging — so multiple agents collaborate through the kernel instead of pasting everything back into one giant prompt.
features: Content-addressed VFS — hash-based change detection skips redundant re-reads
Capability sandbox — least-privilege syscalls, a rogue fs.write outside the jail is denied
Hard credit budgets per process — a runaway agent is stopped, not billed
Semantic memory recall + IPC channels for real multi-agent collaboration
flagship.impact: ~69% fewer credits burned on the same workload, measured

flagship.name: termind
flagship.summary: A private AI agent that lives in your terminal and a Claude-style web UI — one brain, zero cloud dependency, $0 per query.
flagship.description: Runs a local model on-device at zero cost, escalating to a frontier model only on explicit consent with every byte logged. Ships a full agent loop (reason → act → observe), RAG over your own documents with source citations, a database client that previews destructive queries before running them, and a chartered-accountant workbench for regulated data that legally cannot touch the cloud.
features: Think → Act → Observe loop, jailed to a chosen workspace folder
RAG with source citations, DB client with destructive-query preview + confirm gate
Tamper-evident, hash-chained audit ledger of every action taken
Model tiers: local → bigger local → frontier-on-consent, all logged
flagship.impact: Built on AION — the same kernel, applied to a daily-driver agent

flagship.name: rag-from-scratch
flagship.summary: A complete Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline built without LangChain — chunking, embeddings, hybrid retrieval, all understood at the mechanism level.
flagship.description: Three chunking strategies (fixed-size, recursive, sentence-aware), OpenAI embeddings into a FAISS vector index, and a BM25 keyword retriever running in parallel with dense semantic search — fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion so results that rank high by either method rise to the top. Returns grounded answers with the exact source chunks and scores used.
features: Three interchangeable chunkers — fixed, recursive, sentence-based
Hybrid retrieval: dense (FAISS) + lexical (BM25) fused via RRF
Every answer returns its source chunks and relevance scores
A few hundred lines, three dependencies — easy to read end to end
flagship.impact: The reference implementation used to explain RAG mechanics from first principles

flagship.name: langgraph-examples
flagship.summary: ReAct agents, supervisor-led multi-agent systems, human-in-the-loop approval gates, parallel fan-out, self-reflective RAG, and persistent memory — the patterns real agents are built from.
flagship.description: A reference set covering the core LangGraph primitives: nodes that read and update shared state, conditional edges for branching and looping, checkpointed persistence for resumable and human-in-the-loop flows, and prebuilt tool execution. Each example is a runnable, minimal demonstration of one pattern.
features: Supervisor + specialist multi-agent routing
Human-in-the-loop via interrupt_before + checkpointing
Parallel fan-out / fan-in for independent subtasks
Self-reflective RAG that rewrites and re-retrieves on weak context
flagship.impact: Maps directly to LangGraph's actual production API, not toy pseudocode

flagship.name: mcp-servers
flagship.summary: Four production-ready MCP servers exposing GitHub, PostgreSQL, web scraping, and the filesystem as secure tools for any MCP-compatible AI client.
flagship.description: Each server implements list_tools and call_tool; the MCP SDK handles the rest. Safe-by-default throughout — Postgres is read-only unless explicitly flagged writable, the filesystem server is sandboxed to one allowed directory and rejects any path traversal attempt, tokens are scoped per server.
features: GitHub Issues — list, create, comment, search
PostgreSQL — schema inspection + read-safe queries by default
Filesystem — sandboxed to a single allowed directory
Web scraper — structured extraction from any page
flagship.impact: Build once, use from Claude Desktop, Cursor, or any MCP client — no bespoke wiring
